title: Say Cheese
novel:
Lily discovered a [[photograph|photograph]] Ted had hidden for years. In it, her face was [[contorted|contort]] into an awful [[grimace|grimace]]. She looked, Marshall kindly said, like a [[gargoyle|gargoyle]].

"[[Delete|delete]] it," Lily demanded.

Ted refused. "It's honest," he said. "It's the real you."

Lily was [[furious|furious]]. She made it her mission to take a [[flattering|flattering]] photo of Ted — one so [[embarrassing|embarrassing]] that he would beg her to delete it.

The war of cameras [[escalated|escalate]]. They snapped photos at every meal, every yawn, every blink. Marshall's friend, who loved the camera a little too much, visited and made everything worse.

Finally Lily [[captured|capture]] the perfect shot: Ted mid-sneeze, eyes closed, mouth open. She held it up, [[triumphant|triumphant]].

Ted stared at it, then burst out laughing. "We're both [[ridiculous|ridiculous]]," he said.

Lily agreed. She deleted both photos that night. Some [[memories|memory]], they decided, were better kept in the heart than on a [[screen|screen]].

photograph.en: a picture made with a camera

grimace.en: an ugly twist of the face

gargoyle.en: an ugly stone face on a building

embarrassing.en: making you feel shy or ashamed

escalate.en: to become more serious or intense

capture.en: to record an image on camera

screen.en: the flat surface of a camera or phone
